root_cause.text: The purgatory entry point derivation logic in `kexec_load_purgatory()` iterates through all executable sections and matches against `e_entry` without preventing multiple matches, causing a WARN when purgatory objects contain multiple executable sections with overlapping `sh_addr` values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the original code at lines 1004-1012 checks `if (sechdrs[i].sh_flags & SHF_EXECINSTR && pi->ehdr->e_entry >= sechdrs[i].sh_addr && ...)` without any guard to prevent re-matching. The fix introduces a `start_fixed` boolean flag and prioritizes matching against the `purgatory_start` symbol (when present) via `kexec_purgatory_find_symbol()`, then only falls back to the `e_entry` check if `!start_fixed`. The patch also changes the final condition from `!WARN_ON(kbuf->image->start != pi->ehdr->e_entry)` to `kbuf->image->start == pi->ehdr->e_entry`, eliminating the WARN trigger and ensuring the entry point is only set once.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extract symbol lookup logic into a dedicated helper function to support purgatory symbol resolution with proper validation and error handling.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `kexec_purgatory_find_symbol()` that searches for a named symbol in the purgatory's ELF symbol table. The function iterates through section headers to find the symbol table (SHT_SYMTAB), validates the associated string table section, and returns a pointer to the matching global symbol or NULL if not found.
intent_record.how: This function enables symbol lookup within the purgatory ELF image by parsing its ELF headers and sections. It validates section indices to prevent out-of-bounds access, filters for global symbols only, and performs string comparison to match symbol names. The function returns a pointer to the symbol entry on success, allowing callers to access symbol metadata (offset, size, section index, etc.) for further processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce local variables to support enhanced ELF symbol and entry point handling in purgatory setup.
intent_record.what: Added four new local variable declarations in the kexec_purgatory_setup_sechdrs function: a const Elf_Sym pointer (entry_sym), a u16 variable (entry_shndx) initialized to 0, an unsigned long variable (entry_off) initialized to 0, and a bool variable (start_fixed) initialized to false.
intent_record.how: These variables are introduced to support tracking and managing ELF symbol information related to purgatory entry points. The initialization of entry_shndx, entry_off, and start_fixed to zero/false establishes default states that will likely be updated later in the function logic to handle symbol resolution and address offset calculations for the purgatory code execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Locate and cache the purgatory entry point symbol's section index and offset to ensure proper handling of the entry point during kexec purgatory setup.
intent_record.what: Added code block that calls kexec_purgatory_find_symbol() to locate the 'purgatory_start' symbol, then conditionally extracts and stores its section index (st_shndx) and value (st_value) into entry_shndx and entry_off variables if the symbol is found.
intent_record.how: This change enables the kexec code to identify and cache the section index and offset of the purgatory entry point symbol before iterating through section headers. This allows subsequent code (in the for loop) to reference these values when processing sections, likely to handle the entry point section specially or validate its properties.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix entry point address calculation in kexec purgatory setup by detecting and recording the correct image start address when the entry section is encountered.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block that checks if the current section is the entry point section, has executable flags, and the entry offset is within bounds. If conditions are met, it sets kbuf->image->start to the calculated memory address and marks start_fixed as true.
intent_record.how: This change enables the kexec purgatory setup to correctly identify and record the entry point address of the executable image before the existing entry point calculation logic runs. It prevents the image start address from being overwritten later by setting the start_fixed flag, ensuring the entry point is properly established when loading a purgatory image.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix purgatory start address adjustment to execute only once by adding a start_fixed guard and removing the inverted WARN_ON logic.
intent_record.what: Modified the conditional logic in kexec_purgatory_setup_sechdrs: added `!start_fixed &&` check at the beginning of the condition, removed the `!WARN_ON()` wrapper and replaced it with a direct equality check `kbuf->image->start == pi->ehdr->e_entry`, and added `start_fixed = true;` assignment after the block executes.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the purgatory start address adjustment from being applied multiple times. Previously, the WARN_ON would trigger if the condition was true but the start address didn't match, allowing the adjustment to execute anyway. Now, the adjustment only executes once (when start_fixed is false and the address matches exactly), and sets start_fixed to true to prevent re-entry. This ensures idempotent behavior and eliminates spurious warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused static function `kexec_purgatory_find_symbol()` to eliminate dead code.
intent_record.what: Removed the static function `kexec_purgatory_find_symbol()` and its documentation comment (55 lines total), which searched for a symbol in the purgatory ELF structure by iterating through symbol tables and string tables.
intent_record.how: This function is no longer called within the codebase. Its removal eliminates unused code that performed ELF symbol lookup operations. Any remaining callers would need to be updated or this function would need to be inlined/replaced elsewhere, but the diff shows it being cleanly deleted without breaking the subsequent `kexec_purgatory_get_symbol_addr()` function.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8652d44f466ad5772e7d1756e9457046189b0dfc
Author: Ricardo Ribalda <ribalda@chromium.org>
Date:   Fri May 19 16:47:36 2023 +0200

    kexec: support purgatories with .text.hot sections
    
    Patch series "kexec: Fix kexec_file_load for llvm16 with PGO", v7.
    
    When upreving llvm I realised that kexec stopped working on my test
    platform.
    
    The reason seems to be that due to PGO there are multiple .text sections
    on the purgatory, and kexec does not supports that.
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a fix to the vulnerable construct. The vulnerability root cause describes that the entry point derivation logic iterates through executable sections and matches against `e_entry` without preventing multiple matches, causing issues when purgatory objects contain multiple executable sections (like .text and .text.hot) with overlapping `sh_addr` values. The patch adds a guard condition `!WARN_ON(kbuf->image->start != pi->ehdr->e_entry)` to the if statement (line 917-918 in the diff). This prevents recalculation of `image->start` if it has already been set to a value different from the initial `pi->ehdr->e_entry`, which prevents the second executable section (.text.hot) from overwriting the correct `image->start` value calculated from the first section (.text). The comment explicitly explains this behavior: 'If the compiler has produced more than one .text section (Eg: .text.hot), they are generally after the main .text section, and they shall not be used to calculate image->start. So do not re-calculate image->start if it is not set to the initial value.' This is the fix being introduced, not a bug being introduced.
